Notebook introduction

This document provides a comprehensive technical overview and usage manual for the **GPU Hardware Instancing Pipeline** ([`Instanced`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts)) in the Retiam Engine.
1. Architectural Overview & Design Philosophy

In traditional graphics architectures, hardware instancing often relies on per-instance vertex buffer attributes (`stepMode: 'instance'`). However, in modern bindless WebGPU architectures, this approach creates pipeline rigidity, forces pipeline rebuilds, and limits dynamic compute shader manipulation.
Retiam employs a **Programmable Vertex-Pulling Storage Architecture**:

items: **Storage Buffer Binding**: Per-instance data is stored in a structured GPU storage buffer (`array<vec4f>`) bound at `@group(3) @binding(10)` or dynamic resource slot.

**Dual-Mode Bit Packing**: The WebGPU built-in `instance_index` is bit-packed to carry both the **bindless state index** and the **local instance index** simultaneously, with dedicated pass discrimination flags.
**Safe Prototype Cloning**: Instancing an entity clones component instances rather than mutating base class prototypes, preventing cross-entity contamination.
**Sub-Pass Discrimination (Bit 30)**: Fills and strokes are rendered through a single uber-shader in **exactly 2 draw calls** for thousands of vector paths.

blocks.text: 2. Dual-Mode Bit Allocation & firstInstance Architecture
Retiam packs entity state indices and local instance indices into the 32-bit `firstInstance` parameter passed to `pass.draw()` or `pass.drawIndexed()`.
Bit Fields:

items: **Bit 31 (Mode Switch)**: `0` = Standard Mode (14-bit instance capacity), `1` = Mega Mode (18-bit instance capacity).
**Bit 30 (`S` - Stroke Flag)**: `0` = Fill / Default Pass, `1` = Stroke / Secondary Pass.
**State Index Bits**: Extracted branchlessly by the WGSL vertex shader to look up `states[state_index]` (matrix transforms, viewport bounds, global paint).
**Local Index Bits**: Extracted branchlessly by the WGSL vertex shader to pull instance offsets, rotations, scales, and colors from the `instances` storage buffer.

3. Storage Buffer Memory Layout
Each instance occupies **12 contiguous 32-bit floats** (48 bytes per instance), organized into three `vec4f` vectors:

cells.text: 3D World translation coordinates $(x, y, z)$ and uniform scale factor.
3D spatial rotation stored as a unit quaternion.

blocks.text: Automated Promotion:

When a `Path` created in `analytical` mode is passed to `new Instanced(path, count)`, [`Instanced.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts#L78-L84) **automatically promotes** the cloned geometry to [`TriangulatedPathGeometry`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/components/geometry/TriangulatedPathGeometry.ts) and [`TriangulatedPathRenderer`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/components/renderers/TriangulatedPathRenderer.ts).

blocks.text: 8. Performance Best Practices

children: For vector paths, always use `method: 'fast'`. The engine will render all $N$ instances in **exactly 2 draw calls** (Fill + Stroke).

If updating thousands of instances on CPU, modify `instanced.instanceData` directly or use `setInstancePosition`/`setInstanceRotation`, then set `instanced.isDirty = true` **once per frame** at the end of the update loop.
For dynamic physics, swarms, or particle simulations exceeding 20,000 entities, bind `instanced.getInstanceGPUBuffer()` to a `ComputeKernel` to achieve zero-CPU-overhead animation.
Clustered shadow casting on thousands of tiny instances can degrade shadow map fill rate. `Instanced.CAST_SHADOW` defaults to `false` to optimize shadow pass throughput.
